objective: Bootstrap the atlas-ai repository and land the three canonical skills (session-start, session-end, checked-loop) as one agent-neutral text each, guarded by a contract test.
problem: The canonical skills live in ~/.pi/agent/skills and only work in pi: their text names pi-specific tools, files and the pi-subagents scout, and hard-codes machine paths and personal projects. atlas-ai must ship one text that works unchanged in Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI and GitHub Copilot in VS Code, for any user.

in: New git repository at ~/sources/atlas-ai with main, develop and feature/neutral-skills
skills/<name>/SKILL.md for session-start, session-end and checked-loop
skills/embed.go and the contract test skills/skills_test.go
out: The live skills in ~/.pi, ~/.claude and ~/.copilot are not modified
No GitHub repository, push or pull request (asked at close)
Go CLI, component installers, agent adapters and release workflow (later features)

constraints: Never build after changes; tests are run with go test
Every step, rule and heuristic of the pi versions is preserved in the neutral rewrite
checked-loop follows the same neutrality contract (user decision of 2026-11-10 after the native review; replaces the earlier byte-identical constraint)
neutrality_contract: Tools are named by base name (mem_context, mem_search, Atlas search/read, index_status, index_repository) under whatever prefix the runtime exposes
Refer to 'this agent's global instructions file' instead of CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md or APPEND_SYSTEM.md
logbook new --tool <agent-name>: the value this agent already uses in the logbook; if the agent has a Stop hook that calls 'logbook hook', use exactly the hook's value
Delegation: if the runtime has a read-only subagent, delegate heavy reconnaissance; otherwise read inline and say so in the briefing
mem_session_end only if the runtime exposes it
No machine paths or personal projects: $ATLAS_VAULT and generic example project names
Frontmatter: name equals the directory and matches ^[a-z0-9-]{1,64}$; description is non-empty and at most 1024 characters
forbidden_tokens_local: Optional private list in skills/forbidden.local.txt (ignored by git, one token per line). The test adds its tokens when the file exists. It holds names that must not be published: private project names, private hosts, machine-specific paths.
